cluster.headline: הבנק ששבר שיאי רווח "מנמק": הסיבה שאנחנו זקוקים לכסף
חצי האמת של מנכ"ל לאומי: מי באמת מממן את רווחי העתק של הבנק?
כמה מהרווח של הבנקים באמת חוזר אלינו? לא מספיק

fetched_notes: n12 article (full): Leumi Q3 net profit ~NIS 3bn (largest ever for an Israeli bank), up ~10.6% YoY (mainly lower tax), pre-tax profit slightly down. Revenue ~NIS 5.9bn flat; net interest income down 4.5% to NIS 4.27bn. Mizrahi-Tefahot profit NIS 1.37bn (-8%), Hapoalim ~NIS 2.4bn. Leumi to distribute ~NIS 1.5bn dividend (half of quarterly profit), ~NIS 300m via buyback. Competition Authority: if household deposit rates tracked large-business rates, bank household profits 2022-2024 would have been ~NIS 20bn lower. Banks paid NIS 2.5bn special tax 2024-2025; Smotrich's proposed 15% excess-profit tax through 2030 was scaled back to NIS 3bn (2026) + NIS 125m (2027). Without 2026 special tax, Leumi's Q3 profit would have been ~NIS 3.3bn. CEO Hanan Friedman (video on X): public benefits because public owns the bank (no controlling shareholder; held by pension/provident funds); retained earnings fund transport/energy/infrastructure projects. themarker counter-article (teaser only, paywalled): profit described as NIS 3bn (largest ever); implies buyback doesn't transfer cash to savers, benefit depends on individual holdings. themarker 'how much comes back to us' article (paywalled): opening para says Leumi Q3 2026 net profit NIS 3bn, up 11% from NIS 2.7bn same quarter last year; dividend NIS 1.5bn.

claims_seed.claim: ynet/n12 framing: Leumi's NIS 3bn profit is "the largest quarterly profit ever recorded by an Israeli bank"
CEO framing: the public (via pension/provident funds) is the real owner/beneficiary of the profit, implying the NIS 3bn 'returns to the public'

themarker headline framing: 'does the 3bn profit really return to the public?' vs CEO's claim — specifically whether the buyback/dividend mechanism meaningfully returns value to ordinary savers vs. shareholders generally
Profit growth figure: up ~10.6% YoY (n12 article) vs. themarker's own figure of 'up 11% from NIS 2.7bn last year' — check consistency
